S56.state: (b) it was unsafe and is fixed; after the fix the remaining reads have a concrete ordering argument (a) for the audited paths
S56.defect: get0_best_issuer_sk evaluated x->ex_flags when no_dup != 0 before any cache build. The ordinary untrusted path builds x first via X509_self_signed, and X509_STORE_CTX_get1_issuer (no_dup == 0) short-circuits the read, but X509_STORE_CTX_set0_trusted_stack installs get1_best_issuer_other_sk -> get0_best_issuer_sk(no_dup = 1) with no earlier build, so a real X509_verify_cert read raced a concurrent first build.
S56.fix: src/x509/x509_vfy.rs:953: get0_best_issuer_sk calls ossl_x509v3_cache_extensions(x) once before the candidate loop when the stack is non-empty. This is the same X509 write lock the builder takes, not a second lock. It is a no-op when EXFLAG_SET is already published; if this thread is first it performs the build before the read.
publication_argument_after_fix: Every extension-cache member and scalar is written only inside ossl_x509v3_cache_extensions while x->lock is held in write mode; EXFLAG_SET is stored last in the same critical section (src/x509/v3_purp.rs:1940).
A second builder observes EXFLAG_SET and performs no writes; the fields are therefore write-once after publication.

Every x509_vfy path that reads ex_flags/altname/akid/skid/nc/crldp unlocked first acquires and releases the same x->lock in the same thread (X509_self_signed, X509_check_ca, X509_check_purpose, check_issued/ossl_x509_likely_issued, or the new get0_best_issuer_sk call). If the reader built first, the writes are its own; otherwise its acquire is the happens-before edge after the builder's release.

build_chain supplies that edge for every chain member before check_extensions, check_name_constraints, internal_verify, the revocation stage and the policy stage run; the trusted-stack path was the one exception and is now covered by the get0_best_issuer_sk call.
scope_limits: X509_set_proxy_pathlen writes ex_pcpathlen without the lock (the authority does too); S56-R3 remains.

The lazily built policy_cache can set EXFLAG_INVALID_POLICY under x->lock after a reader has already released the lock and is reading ex_flags unlocked; it needs X509_V_FLAG_POLICY_CHECK and a concurrent first policy build. Not covered by the argument above.
X509::policy_cache teardown remains outside the seven extension-cache owners (S56-R4).
Cache teardown (X509_free / D2I_PRE) concurrent with readers is a caller lifetime obligation, as in the authority.

S57.state: (b) it was unsafe and is fixed by a layout-identical design change; data-race freedom for the cache bookkeeping is now established within the stated scope
S57.defect: Eviction/removal/flush wrote not_resumable and owner, and insert-UPDATE_TIME/public time setters wrote time/timeout/calc_timeout, all as plain fields under the context write lock, while a thread that already owned a session reference read them through SSL_SESSION_is_resumable, SSL_SESSION_get_time*/set_time*, and ssl_update_cache with no lock. TSan confirmed both races; the owner path also crashed with a NULL dereference because the accessor re-read owner between lock and unlock.
fix: src/ssl/ssl_lib.rs:2666,2738: not_resumable is AtomicI32 and owner is AtomicPtr<SslCtx>.
src/ssl/ssl_lib.rs:2678,2680,2682: time, timeout and calc_timeout are AtomicU64.
The types are layout-identical to the authority's int/OSSL_TIME/pointer fields; no #[repr(C)] layout, size, offset or exported signature changed, and the struct is opaque to C consumers.
All accesses use Ordering::Relaxed: the values are advisory, and the context lock (where an accessor takes it) orders the protected state. No lock was added that the authority does not take.
src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:1703,1782: SSL_SESSION_set_timeout/_set_time_ex load owner exactly once and use that pointer for both the lock and unlock, removing the NULL-dereference window.
scope_limits: owner names a context that can be retired: SSL_CTX_free must not race a session accessor that dereferences owner (the authority's own object-lifetime contract).

The session payload (id, keys, ticket) is immutable only once the session is published into the cache; a caller that concurrently mutates a shared uncached session through a public setter is outside the contract, as in the authority.
Relaxed atomics make the accesses data-race-free but provide no ordering or freshness guarantee beyond the authority's own best-effort bookkeeping.
S30's recorded divergences (callbacks outside the lock, capacity N vs N-1, insertion-order eviction/flush, no internal-lookup bypass, stateful TLS1.2 tickets) remain.

xstandard_table_sync.decision: removed the unsafe impl Sync rather than leaving a caller obligation dressed as a type invariant
xstandard_table_sync.change: src/x509/v3_purp.rs:546: XstandardTable(UnsafeCell<[X509Purpose; 10]>) and unsafe impl Sync are gone; the standard table is static mut XSTANDARD: [X509Purpose; 10] and X509_PURPOSE_get0 reads it through &raw mut.
xstandard_table_sync.why: X509_PURPOSE_add can rewrite a reserved row in place and the accessors hand out *mut rows. Single-threaded use is the authority's own xstandard[] contract and cannot be enforced at the C ABI without changing table semantics. static mut makes the compiler require an unsafe operation for every access and makes no Sync claim at all; the obligation is stated on the accessors, not asserted as an invariant.
xstandard_table_sync.enforcement: compiler-enforced: all access is through unsafe raw-pointer operations; no safe API exposes the table. The single-threaded discipline itself remains a caller obligation and is documented on X509_PURPOSE_add and the module.

loom.reason: The C rwlock cannot be modelled faithfully. CRYPTO_RWLOCK is a hand-rolled std::sync::Mutex + Condvar with handle-based unlock (CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock takes only an opaque pointer) and raw-pointer identity, and the production transition logic is raw C-ABI pointer code. A Loom model would have to reimplement the publication/eviction/key-comparison transitions instead of using the same code, which the task condition forbids. No toy model was written, and no Loom result is claimed.

compatibility_delta.S56: get0_best_issuer_sk now publishes x's extension cache before the no_dup test. The value it then reads is exactly what the check_issued call in the same loop would have published immediately afterwards; no public return value changes for a consistent cache. In the unsynchronized first-build case the authority's own ex_flags value is indeterminate, so this makes the decision deterministic rather than reproducing a torn read.
compatibility_delta.S57: none observable: the fields keep the authority's size, alignment, offset and values; Relaxed atomic accesses compile to the same aligned loads/stores on x86_64. No lock was added that the authority does not take.
compatibility_delta.ABI: unchanged: 0 #[no_mangle], #[repr(C)] or exported-signature diff lines; the allocator seam coordinates and counts are untouched

remaining_unestablished: S56: X509_set_proxy_pathlen's unlocked ex_pcpathlen write (authority behaviour); the lazy policy_cache's EXFLAG_INVALID_POLICY write vs an already-unlocked reader; X509::policy_cache teardown; cache teardown vs concurrent readers is a caller lifetime obligation.
S57: the SSL_CTX lifetime behind owner (free racing an accessor), and concurrent mutation of a shared uncached session's payload; both are caller contracts in the authority as well.
TSan is evidence only for the interleavings these five tests executed. No Miri, ASan, mutation control, Loom model or authority differential was run for S70.
No independent reviewer adjudicated these claims (AGENTS section 15); the author of the fix is the author of the evidence.
No claim is made beyond the extension-cache publication and the session bookkeeping: this is not a SAFE_COMPATIBLE promotion and no consumer family is graduated.
non_claims: A clean TSan run is not a proof of global race-freedom.
The S56 argument is source-path based and covers the extension-cache fields on the audited x509_vfy paths; the stated exceptions remain.
The S57 atomics change the memory model of the access, not the authority's value semantics; it is a recorded safety improvement with no ABI/layout change.
Removing the XstandardTable Sync assertion does not make concurrent purpose-table use safe; it stops the type system from implying that it is.
